title: YouCoded Pages shell — contract

steps.path: Top bar → Pages, a pinned page's button, and an open page
steps.headline: This is what done means for the Pages shell: the button, the library, pinned pages, and an open page.

rows.statement: A permanent Pages button sits between Settings and Projects; each page you pin adds its own button after Projects.
rows.threshold: every button is the same 24 px square as Projects

rows.statement: Up to four pages can be pinned to the top bar.
On a phone, Pages is a row in the ||| menu right after Projects; pinned page buttons do not appear there.
On a phone the library is one column of the same cards, with the bordered ✕ in place of Esc · Back.
Pages come in two kinds: personal pages, and pages that belong to a project.
The built-in Projects screen stays protected; making pages never changes it.
With no pages yet, the library says what a page is in two sentences and offers one Make a page button.
rows.note: we can make this description more interesting. the examples should be things that excite.intrigue the user, like a calendar, a personalized news feed or email browser, or an app to manage their team's timesheets.

rows.statement: The welcome card names pages worth wanting: a calendar, a news feed, an email browser, a team timesheet.
Each library card carries an upright push-pin, filled in when the page is pinned and an outline when not.
Edit in chat is only on the library cards, a pencil beside the pin with a hover tip; the open page has none.
The Week planner sample shows seven day columns, events coloured by kind, done or to do, and a quick add.
Paint studio has tools left, palette and brush settings right, undo and redo; its paper stays white in every theme.
The panel beside an open page lists every page, with its pin beside each one.
Manage pages, at the bottom of the panel, opens the full Pages screen.
Esc, or Back to chat at the top right, leaves the open page.
The panel is its own rounded pane, like the files and games pane in chat; Manage pages fills its width at the bottom.
The panel collapses with the button at the top-left of the page view, and the page takes the full width.
rows.note: again this frame is kinda weird with a separate divider layer under the title? the edge of the frame itself should be the divier.

rows.statement: With the panel collapsed, the page pane keeps the same edge all round instead of touching the window.
The band above a page: panel toggle, page name, Back to chat and window buttons, all in the same quiet inset style.
rows.threshold: nothing on the band has an outline
rows.note: this looks weird, the back to chat/esc arent aligned. and we should add a dot or something between them

rows.statement: Back to chat and Esc share one baseline at the same size, with a dot between them.
The library header is the title left, Make a page and Esc · Back right; cards group under Personal, then each project.
The band has no line under it, the page's name sits in the exact centre, and the panel starts hidden.
With the panel shown, panel and page are two rounded panes inset by the same edge on every side.
rows.threshold: 10 px edge on every side; panel 240 px

rows.statement: Clicking a page in the panel opens it in place; the band's name and icon follow.
